fields.logicalExtension.pro.newArguments.0.text: A morally defensible accommodation must contain an internal mechanism that reduces dependence on the tolerated wrong. Read cumulatively, release provisions, fugitive refuge, redemption rights, manumission practices, and shared worship constitute institutional pressure toward freedom rather than mere regulation of permanent domination. This trajectory is measurable: where a passage provides no avenue of exit, the accommodation account faces an especially serious difficulty, because constraint without any path beyond bondage does not yet explain how toleration is ordered toward abolition.
fields.logicalExtension.pro.newArguments.1.text: Surface legal permission need not define a canon’s governing moral norm. Interpretations should instead be tested for coherence with creation, liberation, neighbor-love, and equal standing before God; if those themes have independently justified priority, particular permissions are properly read narrowly as emergency governance rather than timeless authorization. Yet that priority must be applied consistently to the hardest case, permanent foreign slavery. Invoking moral unity only when a text becomes embarrassing would beg the question rather than establish the claimed hierarchy of norms.
